speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please tell me how old you are and at what age you experienced your first menstrual period, if at all? Additionally, have you ever broken a bone from a minor fall or everyday activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of primary amenorrhea, ambiguous genitalia at birth, and bone fragility, I need to assess your current physical development. Can you describe your current breast development stage and whether you have any pubic or axillary hair? Additionally, what is your current height and how does it compare to your parents' heights?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any dark, coarse hair on your face, chest, or abdomen, and are you currently taking any medications other than isotretinoin and oral contraceptives? I would also like to know if you have experienced any episodes of low blood sugar or seizures, as this could help clarify the underlying hormonal imbalance. REQUEST TEST: 17-OH Progesterone

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the 17-OH progesterone is normal, that effectively rules out classic Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia. Given the bone fragility and ambiguous genitalia, I need to check your blood pressure to see if you might have 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency, which can cause hypertension. Do you have a history of high blood pressure or headaches? REQUEST TEST: Plasma Aldosterone

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal 17-OH progesterone and aldosterone, classic CAH is unlikely, so I need to evaluate for other causes of virilization and bone issues. Do you have a family history of similar symptoms, and have you ever experienced episodes of low blood sugar or abdominal pain? REQUEST TEST: Serum Testosterone and LH/FSH

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum Testosterone: 150 ng/dL (Elevated), LH: 0.5 mIU/mL (Suppressed), FSH: 1.2 mIU/mL (Low)

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated testosterone with suppressed LH and FSH points towards an androgen-secreting tumor or a rare form of CAH, but the normal 17-OH progesterone makes typical 21-hydroxylase deficiency unlikely. I need to check for other enzyme deficiencies that cause virilization without hypertension. REQUEST TEST: Serum 11-Deoxycorticosterone and Urinary 17-Ketosteroids

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated 11-deoxycorticosterone confirms 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency, which explains the virilization and bone fragility due to chronic androgen excess. DIAGNOSIS READY: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency
